title: How We Define Harm Impacts Data Annotations: Explaining How Annotators Distinguish Hateful, Offensive, and Toxic Comments
reasoning: The paper focuses on the technical and linguistic definitions used in data annotation for harmful content detection. While it touches on categories of harm that have moral dimensions (e.g., hate speech), it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, faith, or specific ethical/moral systems. It is an empirical study of annotation methodology and rater behavior.
